title: MK Stalin concedes defeat, says DMK will work as exemplary Opposition
byline: MK Stalin has conceded defeat in the Tamil Nadu election, accepting the verdict of the people and congratulating the winning side. “We bow to and accept the verdict of the people. Congratulations to the victors!” Stalin said in a post on X, acknowledging the outcome after a closely watched contest in the southern state.

title: Sri Lanka Cricket Transformation Committee members receive appointment letters
byline: The official appointment letters for members of the newly established Cricket Transformation Committee (CTC) were handed over today by Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports, Sunil Kumara Gamage.

title: Hot, humid weather to end by mid-May: Met. Dept.
byline: The current hot, humid weather, which causes excess perspiration, is expected to end by the middle of this month with the onset of the southwest monsoon, the Department of Meteorology said today.

title: PM Modi hails historic win in West Bengal and Assam
byline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) headquarters in New Delhi on Monday as counting trends showed the party surging past the majority mark in West Bengal and retaining power in Assam.

title: UAE says Iran fired drones at oil tanker in Hormuz
byline: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) says Iran launched two suicide drones at a tanker affiliated with its Abu Dhabi National Oil Company in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: US denies Iranian claim it struck American warship
byline: US Central Command (Centcom) denies that one of its warships has been struck by two Iranian missiles.

title: Cabinet clears major contracts to upgrade Southern highway corridor
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved two major contracts under the National Highways Widening and Improvement Programme to rehabilitate key sections of the Colombo–Galle–Hambantota–Wellawaya (A002) Road, aimed at strengthening connectivity along the southern corridor.

title: Treasury Secretary not a dual citizen, Minister Jayatissa
byline: Dismissing growing speculation, Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said Finance Ministry Secretary Harshana Suriyapperuma was not a dual citizen during his time in public office.

title: Iranian foreign minister heads to China for talks
byline: Abbas Araghchi will travel to Beijing later today for discussions.

title: Menzies Aviation wins SriLankan contract at Sydney Airport
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to award the contract for ground handling services for SriLankan Airlines at Sydney Airport in Australia. This decision follows the expiration of the previous service agreement on April 30, 2026.

title: Ravi K proposes Speaker to use official residence
byline: Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekara alleged that Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne is using the Speaker’s official residence and another apartment in the apartment complex belonging to the Ministry of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government, despite claims of not using any residences.

title: PET scan services to resume after shortage of key chemical resolved
byline: PET scan services, which had been suspended since March 27 due to a shortage of the radioactive chemical FDG, are set to resume from tomorrow (May 6).

title: Middle East truce in doubt as US and Iran fight for control of Strait of Hormuz
byline: A fragile truce in the Middle East was under strain on Tuesday after the U.S. and Iran exchanged fire ​in the Gulf as they wrestled for control of the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Sri Lanka captain closes in on No.1 ranking ahead of T20WC
byline: Eye-catching gains on the updated T20I rankings for a host of players from Sri Lanka and Bangladesh with just over a month until the T20 World Cup.

title: Urgent debate in Parliament today on disappearance of USD 2.5 million from Treasury
byline: The government today agreed to grant an urgent debate on the disappearance of USD 2.5 million from the Treasury, following a request by the Opposition.

title: Namal congratulates Vijay on TN election win
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and MP Namal Rajapaksa has congratulated actor-turned-politician C. Joseph Vijay on his reported victory in the Tamil Nadu elections.

title: Sandwich boys exploited by sadism at schools rugby
byline: First came the purported attack on a rugby referee in a mafia like pursuit by a group of thugs on motorcycles.

title: One clause of Inland Revenue Amendment Bill inconsistent with Constitution
byline: The Supreme Court has determined that Clause 34(1) of the Inland Revenue Amendment Bill is inconsistent with the Constitution, Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne announced in Parliament today.

title: India-Sri Lanka land bridge: time for wavering over: Indian envoy
byline: Indian High Commissioner Santosh Jha renewed the call for the need to build a land link between Sri Lanka and India and said the time for wavering is over.

title: Court orders forensic analysis in case involving minor
byline: The Anuradhapura Chief Magistrate Siyapath Sasindu Wickramaratne yesterday directed the Gampaha Division Police Children and Women’s Bureau to submit case materials to the Government Analyst and present the report to court in connection with an alleged abuse case involving a 15-year-old girl, reportedly implicating a Buddhist monk and several other individuals.

title: Galle Prison under fire after underworld celebration video leaks
byline: A viral video showing an alleged birthday celebration inside the high-security Galle Prison has triggered public concern and prompted an official investigation into possible security lapses and breaches of prison regulations.

title: Rejection of Sri Lankan student visa applications to Australia surge to 38%
byline: Sri Lankan students are increasingly affected by the impact of Australia’s tightened student visa policies, with new data showing a significant rise in rejection rates for higher education visas.

title: President faces contempt of court allegations over remarks on May 25 judgment
byline: Riled by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s claim that he had prior knowledge of a judgment to be delivered on May 25, the Joint Opposition is now planning to address a letter to the Chief Justice, drawing his attention to this very distressing situation.

title: Sri Lanka named priority country in U.S. Food for Progress funding for 2026
byline: The United States Department of Agriculture’s Foreign Agricultural Service has officially designated Sri Lanka as a priority country for its Food for Progress programme in the upcoming 2026 fiscal year.

title: Sajith should act as Opposition Leader, not as SJB leader: Joint Opposition
byline: Sajith Premadasa should act as the Opposition Leader and should work with all Opposition political parties, former Minister Dilan Perera said on behalf of the Joint Opposition.

title: Special Parliamentary Committee appointed to review election laws
byline: A special Parliamentary committee chaired by Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government Dr. A.H.M.H. Abayarathna has been appointed to review and make recommendations on laws pertaining to elections, except for laws pertaining to the Provincial Council elections.

title: 37 Chinese nationals arrested in Negombo deported under tight security
byline: A group of 37 Chinese nationals who had entered Sri Lanka on business visas and were allegedly hiding in a house in the Negombo area were deported late last night following their arrest by immigration authorities.

title: Explosion at China fireworks factory kills 21 people
byline: A blast at a fireworks factory in China’s Hunan province has killed 21 people and left 61 wounded, according to state media.

title: VAT revision not a tax increase, govt. clarifies tax change
byline: Deputy Minister of Economic Development Nishantha Jayaweera yesterday rejected claims of a looming VAT hike, stating that tax changes due to take effect on July 1, 2026, are intended to streamline the system without increasing the overall tax burden.

title: Sri Lanka’s new VAT rules could have negative outcome on tourism, telecom, IT sectors
byline: The government’s latest move to expand the Value Added Tax (VAT) net to the digital economy, effective July 1, has triggered alarm bells across multiple sectors.

title: US strikes Iranian fast boats as Iran attacks UAE oil facility
byline: President Donald Trump says the US has struck seven Iranian ’’fast boats’’ in the Strait of Hormuz, as Washington seeks to guide stranded ships out of the Gulf through the largely closed waterway.

title: Tamil Nadu election results final: TVK shocks Dravidian giants, looks to form govt amidst fractured verdict
byline: While Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) president C Joseph Vijay began his journey to the chief minister’s office at For St George on Monday, Tamil Nadu entered an uncharted political territory of a fractured mandate and the possibility of a coalition govt.

title: India trade push could boost Sri Lanka exports by half: ADB
byline: Sri Lanka could expand its exports by as much as 50 percent by deepening the trade ties with India, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) said, while it went on to warn that the island nation’s continued reliance on the Western markets is leaving it exposed to external shocks and constraining growth.

title: Hambantota International Port attracts major global shipping lines
byline: Hambantota International Port Group (HIPG) last week hosted senior representatives from two of the world’s leading container shipping lines, signalling growing commercial interest in the port as global trade patterns adjust to instability in the Middle East.

title: SriLankan Airlines partners with Flynas to boost Saudi connectivity
byline:
SriLankan Airlines has entered into a partnership with Saudi Arabia’s Flynas to enhance air connectivity between the two countries, with the aim of offering the passengers more convenient travel options across key routes.
The alliance is aimed at improving access for tourists, business travellers and pilgrims by enabling smoother connections between international and domestic flights.

title: ’I won’t resign, we haven’t lost’: Mamata Banerjee rejects Bengal verdict
byline: Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday said she will not resign as West Bengal Chief Minister, asserting that she does not accept the election outcome as a legitimate defeat and will continue her political fight despite the setback.

title: Action against two non-parliamentary personalities who gave publicity to USD 2.5 million heist
byline: Action will be taken against two non-parliamentary personalities who have caused distress to the family of State official Ranga Rajapaksa who was found dead after the alleged heist of USD 2.5 million was revealed, a senior Minister told Parliament today.

title: Fertilizer Secretariat denies claims of excessive urea prices
byline: The National Fertilizer Secretariat has rejected allegations that the government procured urea fertilizer at inflated prices, dismissing claims made by a representative of the National Farmers’ Collective.

title: US says Iran ceasefire holds despite exchange of fire in Gulf
byline: Washington said Iran had not breached a fragile ceasefire in the Middle East ​conflict on Tuesday, following an exchange of fire between the two sides the previous day as U.S. forces attempted to force open the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Should SLR invest more on 7s?
byline: The Sri Lanka rugby team was once again easily beaten by New Zealand Under 85kg in Kandy last weekend. Sri Lanka was beaten by 27 points to 16 points in the first game and then they were handed a defeat of 25 points to 10 in the second game.

title: Market retreats amid renewed geopolitical concerns
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange ended today’s session on a negative note, with both indices closing in red territory as renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East weighed on investor sentiment. The negative external backdrop led to a gradual decline in confidence, resulting in subdued trading activity throughout the session.

title: Group of MPs to petition President
byline: Around 25 MPs representing various parties in the opposition is to send in a petition to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake asking him to respect the Judiciary and uphold its independence.

title: Human-to-human transmission suspected on board hantavirus cruise ship, WHO says
byline: Some human-to-human transmission may have occurred on board the cruise ship hit by a hantavirus outbreak that has left three people dead and several others ill, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Tuesday.

title: PUCSL to review 2026 electricity tariff due to price hike concerns
byline: The Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) is set to hold a stakeholder consultation tomorrow on the proposed Extraordinary Electricity Tariff Review for 2026, amid growing public concern over potential increases in electricity charges.

title: Namal calls for govt. intervention over attack on Jaffna fisherman
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organizer Namal Rajapaksa today raised a serious concern in Parliament regarding a Sri Lankan fisherman from Palali, Jaffna, who was allegedly assaulted and abducted and is now receiving medical treatment in Chennai, India.

title: Heavy rain expected islandwide from tomorrow
byline: The Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), where winds from the Northern and Southern Hemispheres converge, is expected to significantly influence weather conditions over Sri Lanka, leading to an increase in rainfall from tomorrow (06), the Meteorology Department said.

title: Government resumes stalled archaeological restoration work: Minister
byline: The current government has resumed restoration work on several archaeological sites that had been previously stalled, Buddhist Studies, Religious and Cultural Affairs Minister Dr. Hiniduma Sunil Senavi said.

title: President’s statement on judicial decision erodes public confidence in the Judiciary: BASL
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has expressed grave concern over remarks made by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake during his recent May Day rally, warning that such statements could undermine public confidence in the judiciary.

title: Money for officials, nothing for players
byline: Sri lanka’s boys and girls who skipped Academic Studies Deprived of Competing at Asian Volleyball as Ministry says no funds for the National Sport.

title: Govt weighs tough curbs on children’s screen time
byline: The government is mulling imposing stricter regulations on children’s use of digital devices and social media amid growing concerns over exploitation, addiction, and behavioural issues linked to unsupervised access, Women and Child Affairs Minister Saroja Savithri Paulraj said.

title: US says Iran ceasefire holds despite exchange of fire in Gulf
byline: Washington said Iran had not breached a fragile ceasefire in the Middle East ​conflict on Tuesday, following an exchange of fire between the two sides the previous day as U.S. forces attempted to force open the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Human-to-human transmission suspected on board hantavirus cruise ship, WHO says
byline: Some human-to-human transmission may have occurred on board the cruise ship hit by a hantavirus outbreak that has left three people dead and several others ill, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Tuesday.
